# zla_wwaddw

> Adds a complex vector in doubled-single precision representation.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlaWwaddw from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zla_wwaddw';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zla_wwaddw( N, x, strideX, y, strideY, w, strideW ) → Complex128Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of elements |
| `x` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · High-order part of the doubled-single accumulation vector |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride length for `x` |
| `y` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Low-order part of the doubled-single accumulation vector |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | Stride length for `y` |
| `w` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Vector to be added |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride length for `w` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The length of vectors X, Y, and W.
- `x`: The first part of the doubled-single accumulation vector.
- `y`: The second part of the doubled-single accumulation vector.
- `w`: The vector to be added.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: `x`

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zla_wwaddw.strided(
    N,
    x, strideX, offsetX,
    y, strideY, offsetY,
    w, strideW, offsetW
) → Complex128Array
```

Adds a complex vector W into a doubled-single accumulation vector (X, Y).

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Length of vectors X, Y, and W |
| `x` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · First part of the doubled-single accumulation vector |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride length for `x` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `x` (in complex elements) |
| `y` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Second part of the doubled-single accumulation vector |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | Stride length for `y` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetY` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `y` (in complex elements) |
| `w` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Vector to be added |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride length for `w` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetW` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `w` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The length of vectors X, Y, and W.
- `x`: The first part of the doubled-single accumulation vector.
- `y`: The second part of the doubled-single accumulation vector.
- `w`: The vector to be added.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: `x`

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zla_wwaddw()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZLA_WWADDW`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zla_wwaddw.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import uniform from '@stdlib/random/array/uniform/lib/index.js';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import zlaWwaddw from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zla_wwaddw';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;

// Doubled-single accumulator `x + y` (high-order part `x`, low-order part `y`) and the vector `w` to add:
const x = new Complex128Array( uniform( 2 * N, -10.0, 10.0, opts ) );
const y = new Complex128Array( N );
const w = new Complex128Array( uniform( 2 * N, -10.0, 10.0, opts ) );

// Using the standard interface:
zlaWwaddw( N, x, 1, y, 1, w, 1 );
console.log( reinterpret( x, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the strided interface:
zlaWwaddw.strided( N, x, 1, 0, y, 1, 0, w, 1, 0 );
console.log( reinterpret( x, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZLA_WWADDW`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZLA\_WWADDW adds a vector W into a doubled-single vector (X, Y).

This works for all extant IBM's hex and binary floating point arithmetic, but not for decimal.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
